policy: Keep exact manufacturer model identities in this unified database even while research is incomplete. Use verified only when ratings, colors, terminal layouts, and installation guidance are sourced; otherwise use partially verified or reference only, list missingData, and never infer unknown values.

rules.text: Mount vertically on a non-flammable surface with electrical terminals facing down. Keep at least 100 mm clearance above and below for cooling.
Mount within 3 m of the battery, but not directly above it.
Protect the battery supply with a fuse selected from the exact model's manual table. This database does not substitute a fuse rating.

Keep array open-circuit voltage at or below the exact model limit and nominal PV voltage at least 5 V above battery voltage. Account for cold-weather Voc rise and the panel voltage temperature coefficient.

Check polarity, connect the battery first, allow 10 seconds for automatic voltage detection, then connect the DC load and PV. PV-first connection is allowed only when system voltage was manually configured first.
Use flexible multi-stranded copper for screw connections and torque battery, load, and PV terminals to 0.75 N·m.

The PV input is not isolated from the battery circuit and the controller has no internal ground-fault protection. Follow the exact manual and applicable local requirements for enclosures, disconnection, grounding, and any required external protection.
Mount upright or on its side, but never with the battery terminals facing down. The 12.8 V/330 Ah model is upright-only.
Size battery cables for expected current and fuse every battery cable. The fuse rating must not exceed the lowest applicable cable, battery, or system current rating.
Observe battery polarity, prevent terminal short circuits, and tighten connection bolts to the torque specified in the manual using insulated tools.
Use matching battery models and capacities in a bank where possible; follow the manual's limits and wiring guidance for series and parallel connections.
Mount vertically on a non-flammable surface with electrical terminals facing down. Keep at least 100 mm clearance above and below for cooling.
Mount within 3 m of the battery, but not directly above it.
Protect the battery supply with a fuse selected from the exact model's manual table. This database does not substitute a fuse rating.

Keep array open-circuit voltage at or below 100 V and nominal PV voltage at least 5 V above battery voltage. Account for cold-weather Voc rise and the panel voltage temperature coefficient; do not use PV optimizers.
Check polarity, connect the battery first, allow 10 seconds for automatic voltage detection, then connect PV. PV-first connection is allowed only when system voltage was manually configured first.
Use flexible multi-stranded copper for screw connections and torque battery and PV terminals to 1.6 N·m.

The PV input is not isolated from the battery circuit and the controller has no internal ground-fault protection. Follow the exact manual and applicable local requirements for enclosures, disconnection, grounding, and any required external protection.
Install as a surface-mounted circuit breaker using its specified mounting arrangement.
Use 1/4-inch ring terminals on the M6 studs and tighten the terminal hardware to 50 in-lb (5.65 N·m).
Do not use this circuit breaker as a switch where high inrush current is expected.
The six controller terminals are arranged along the bottom in this left-to-right order: PV positive, PV negative, battery positive, battery negative, load positive, load negative.
Keep PV open-circuit voltage at or below 100 V and maximum array power within the documented battery-voltage limit: 520 W at 12 V or 1040 W at 24 V.
Follow the manual's battery-first wiring sequence and its model-specific cable and fuse sizing guidance; this catalogue does not replace local electrical requirements.
Keep cold-corrected PV open-circuit voltage within the 120 V controller limit. Size PV over-current protection, battery protection, and conductors to the exact controller model and applicable code.
The main bottom terminals are arranged left to right as Solar +/−, Load +/−, and Battery +/−. The wiring diagram also shows separate voltage-sense and temperature-sensor connections.
The manual specifies PV-input over-current ratings of 40 A for PS-MPPT-25 and 50 A for PS-MPPT-40; do not apply one model's value to another.
Keep cold-corrected PV open-circuit voltage within the exact model limit: 60 V for the 06 models and 100 V for the 10 models.
The six main terminals are on the bottom. The manual groups them as PV, battery, and load connections; wire them using the labeled polarity on the device and its model manual.
Use the manual's specified external fast-acting protection and installation environment; isolate the PV array and battery before adjustment or wiring.
Do not exceed the module's 1000 V maximum system voltage; array design must also account for cold-corrected open-circuit voltage and applicable electrical requirements.
Use compatible PV-ST01 / MC4-type connectors as identified by the manufacturer and preserve module polarity when connecting the array.
Use DC battery cables and connections sized for the inverter's current; keep polarity correct and consult the exact model manual for cable and over-current protection sizing.
Use the correct regional AC output socket and frequency for the exact model; this record represents the 230 V, 50 Hz variant.
